concepts.title: Deployed components and shared infrastructure
concepts.rationale: Preserve the canonical component identity and PNG. Correct Worker x1 to the configured two-replica floor (HPA 2–3); remove MCP CSI and AgentHost-to-Key-Vault authority arrows; label SecretProviderClass separately from the actual vault. API and Worker both use the durable EF store, not an API-read/Worker-write partition. Distinguish Copilot credential delivery from repository operations and show the preview gateway as a separate ingress plane rather than suggesting every browser path uses the application gateway.

concepts.title: Claim, configure, readiness, turns and release
concepts.rationale: Keep the lifecycle diagram but replace KV-secret metadata with the purpose-bound launch contract, add claim binding before configuration, and make readiness depend on the ready response rather than HTTP 200: /healthz returns 200 in standby too. Preserve one-time configuration/409, shared versus local-read-only workspace semantics, and the possibility of retaining an Assistant pod between turns; do not imply every turn ends by deleting a claim.

concepts.title: Gateway routing and effective network-policy boundaries
concepts.rationale: The embedded alt text promises client/LB/Service routing, but the source is an egress-policy topology. Reconcile these as the single network canonical: show Gateway→HTTPRoute→Service→pod, exact application/OAuth/MCP routes, and separate preview ingress. Remove MCP CSI and sandbox vault-token-fetch paths. Include AgentHost→API/MCP selector-based TCP 8080 and public HTTPS with private/link-local exclusions; do not claim Kata egress is FQDN-only. Reuse this canonical for the empty Gateway API resource relationships and Network traffic diagram headings instead of adding another graph.

concepts.title: Network policies, runtime isolation and external dependencies
concepts.rationale: Keep the policy and dependency tables as precise reference material, with factual corrections rather than another image. The sandbox selector is now app: agentweaver-agent-host, the public-HTTPS rule is not a GitHub-only /20, preview ingress is another exception, and the effective Kata boundary cannot be described as an additional FQDN restriction. Explicitly distinguish network reachability from Key Vault authorization and kubelet image pull.

concepts.title: Separate workload identities and brokered credential delivery
concepts.rationale: The legacy source gives the AgentHost ServiceAccount the API managed identity and a direct SecretClient/KeyVaultUserTokenProvider path. Replace this with API/Worker federation to the privileged identity, a distinct AgentHost identity with no Key Vault role, and the API-side run-bound capability broker followed by one-time configuration. MCP has no mounted secrets. Keep OAuth certificate-family loading distinct from CSI app-secret delivery.

concepts.title: Durable database, shared workspace and startup migrations
concepts.rationale: Keep the compact workspace directory tree and accompanying connection/migration tables; these do not need a PNG. Correct the production SqliteDb/Dapper split to current EF-backed stores. Distinguish shared /workspace from the already documented local-read-only assembly checkout; schema configuration and init-container ordering are more useful as executable/text reference than another component diagram.

concepts.title: Entra sign-in versus MCP and GitHub capabilities
concepts.rationale: Keep deployment-specific callback/origin instructions, but refer to the authentication guide's authoritative capability hierarchy rather than maintaining a second simplified project-Copilot-only login model. No foreign canonical is edited.

concepts.title: Personal sessions, durable replay, resume and deletion
concepts.rationale: The short user-oriented lifecycle is clearer as prose than another runtime diagram. Correct the advertised three active sessions to the configured default five; retain 30-minute idle completion, durable replay and resume semantics. Do not depict project association as session ownership.

concepts.title: Per-turn MCP authorization and personal provider resolution
concepts.rationale: Reuse the provider hierarchy explanation instead of adding a competing authentication graph. The five-minute per-turn MCP broker is supported; the assertion that an AgentHost session must start in a Copilot-connected project is stale. Accepted assistant_turn execution plans and platform/non-project fallback are not a requirement for project-scoped Copilot.

concepts.title: Entra, browser session, bearer token and hosted MCP OAuth
concepts.rationale: Retain the explicit distinctions between platform identity, opaque cookie, tab-local bearer, pinned public origin and exact MCP resource. The ordered sign-in/setup/sign-out guidance is usable without a separate image; link MCP consent mechanics rather than drawing GitHub as the identity provider.

concepts.title: Project/background versus personal-session provider hierarchy
concepts.rationale: Make this the guide-level canonical explanation, preferably with a small decision table: active project binding wins and fails closed if stale; absent project binding inherits platform BYOK then platform Copilot; personal sessions use platform BYOK, personal BYOK, then personal Copilot. Repo access is separate. Current ordered prose already covers these branches, so do not commission a duplicate graphic solely to fill empty space.

concepts.title: Exact callbacks, shared registration migration and safe completion
concepts.rationale: Retain literal callback URLs, ordered migration steps and safe completion guidance as text. Three completion scopes now share the Copilot callback (project, platform, personal user); the MCP browser handoff is an entry point rather than a fourth callback. Do not reproduce configuration.md's older two-flow claim.

concepts.title: Library-first generation, validation and safe apply
concepts.rationale: Keep this concise validation checklist instead of a new diagram: required fields, known or declared bespoke roles, connected runnable workflows and supported sandbox profiles have direct implementation checks. Clarify that the currently accepted review policy is default, not an open catalog of policies. Preserve the generate→validate→edit/regenerate→apply distinction.

concepts.title: Actual Kanban board presentation
concepts.rationale: The referenced board.png is a 70-byte 1×1 PNG, not a usable screenshot. Recapture the current UI, including its main Backlog/Ready/Active/Done row and separate attention section, or remove the placeholder embed. This is screenshot remediation, not draw.io authoring.

concepts.title: Six semantic buckets and user-versus-coordinator transitions
concepts.rationale: Continue reusing the shared canonical, not a guide-specific copy. Correct the Problems→Ready drag instructions at line 88: current drag handlers and tests allow Backlog↔Ready only. Keep semantic columns separate from their physical layout and use explicit retry controls for failed runs.

concepts.title: Capture, rank, preview decomposition, confirm and heartbeat pickup
concepts.rationale: Keep operational steps and settings in prose/table form. Explicitly distinguish decomposition preview from confirm=true persistence, and pickup autopilot from tool approval and manual starts. The common canonical board graphic need not expand into a settings reference.

Repair the OAuth table interrupted by prose before LifetimeDays so the remaining rows render as a table.

Correct 'exactly two' Copilot completion flows to include personal-user consent; refer to the authentication hierarchy instead of implying platform Copilot supplies personal chat.

concepts.title: Provision versus deploy-local/commit/release versus verify
concepts.rationale: Retain executable command recipes with a small command-choice table rather than a new pipeline image. findings.subject: AKS visuals assert obsolete privileged AgentHost and MCP secret paths
findings.detail: Three owned sources show AgentHost Key Vault access and/or MCP CSI mounts despite separate unprivileged AgentHost identity and an empty MCP volumeMounts list. The secrets source explicitly names KeyVaultUserTokenProvider and routes AgentHost federation into the API managed identity. These must not be republished as current architecture. Correct implementation-backed authority boundaries before visual authoring; this audit makes no claim about live-deployment security.

findings.subject: All eleven guide screenshot embeds point to 1×1 placeholders
findings.detail: PNG IHDR inspection found all eleven referenced guide UI images are 70 bytes, 1×1 pixels, with the same SHA-256 prefix 6b7fa434f92a8b80. They exist, so link checks alone would miss the absence of useful visual coverage. Recapture or remove these placeholders in a separately authorized screenshot task. PNG dimensions were inspected programmatically; rendered UI/image appearance was not inspected. Unreferenced casting-wizard.png and sign-in.png have the same placeholder dimensions.

findings.subject: Network prose, graph scope and deployed policies diverge
findings.detail: The network alt text describes an inbound client/LB/service path while its source is a policy graph. Empty headings remain for Gateway API relationships and a network traffic diagram. The sandbox policy table uses the old selector and GitHub-only CIDR; current manifests select agentweaver-agent-host, allow preview-gateway ingress 3000–9000, narrow selector-based API/MCP egress, and public HTTPS excluding private/link-local ranges. The Kata policy comments explicitly explain why FQDN-only enforcement is not the effective boundary.

findings.subject: Worker and persistence facts are stale
findings.detail: The component source says Worker x1 and assigns database reads to API and writes to Worker. Current Worker base replicas are two, HPA bounds are 2–3, and autoscaling uses CPU 70% plus memory 80%; operations.md describes CPU-only scaling. The AKS guide also describes a SqliteDb/Dapper plus EF split while current production registration uses EF-backed project/run stores.

findings.subject: Warm-pool readiness is not HTTP-200 readiness
findings.detail: The lifecycle source labels Ready with /healthz 200, but the endpoint always returns 200 after Kestrel starts, with standby or ready content. A future diagram must show readiness after setup, not a status-code-only gate that could teach a deadlock or premature turn dispatch.

findings.subject: Child RAI and preview ownership descriptions conflict with current execution
findings.detail: Example scenarios and the overview alt text still show per-child RAI, and runs.md later repeats that each agent passes RAI despite its correct Agent→Assemble-ready text diagram. Child RunWorkflowFactory bypasses RAI entirely; collective software gates order RAI before Build & Test. Build/test no longer asks the agent to call start_preview: deterministic PreviewStep runs afterward. Shared diagram owners must reconcile these facts, including the proposed guide review merge.

findings.subject: Backlog examples teach unsupported or duplicate launch transitions
findings.detail: Problems→Ready dragging is documented in two pages but current board handlers/tests constrain dragging to Backlog↔Ready. mcp-cli.md chains Ready pickup with run_task even though run_task starts another coordinator. Spec decomposition also needs a clear preview→confirm persistence boundary rather than saying all proposed items are immediately added.

findings.subject: Assistant and configuration provider descriptions lag current hierarchy
findings.detail: Assistant guide says three active sessions and requires a project Copilot connection for AgentHost mode; current options/config default to five and assistant accepted plans/non-project fallback do not impose that project prerequisite. Configuration says exactly two shared Copilot callback completion flows despite the personal UserCopilot flow, and its provider table still attributes run tokens to the signed-in user's session. Reuse authentication.md's project-versus-personal hierarchy.

findings.subject: MCP lifecycle graphic does not use the exact documented tool
findings.detail: guide-example-scenarios-fig3 labels the gate outcome_spec_confirm, while the actual tool is coordinator_outcome_spec_confirm. Replace work_plan + children with exact tool names, retain the stable PNG and reuse this corrected lifecycle from mcp-cli.md.

findings.subject: Release/cutover prose requires explicit historical scope
findings.detail: The Fleet matrix retains foundation-only coverage language and an absolute process credential assertion while current AgentHost declares a run-scoped repository credential. Treat this as a source-backed contract reconciliation, not a security verdict. Operations rollback must also respect the matrix's irreversible-cleanup boundary. Getting-started's four blocking checks is stale against the current required seven .NET shard contexts plus other suites.

findings.subject: Consolidation plan and research-only limitations
findings.detail: All 20 assigned pages and six owned diagram sources were read. Prose, tables, inline tool/ASCII chains, code examples, image links and provenance were assessed; no inline Mermaid, HTML image/SVG or iframe visual was found on these pages. Five owned diagrams require redesign; guide-review-fig1 is a cross-owner merge candidate into canonical-default-workflow. Existing board, coordinator, sandbox, workflow-authoring, selection, invocation and memory canonicals are named reuse targets only; foreign entries were not edited. No pitch, iteration, rendering, deployed UI validation, PNG appearance inspection or runtime test execution occurred. This report is bounded research, not final catalog publication approval.
